title: Continued Rapid Radio Brightening of the Tidal Disruption Event AT2018hyz
question: What is the physical origin and geometry of the continued, rapidly rising late-time radio and millimeter emission from the tidal disruption event AT2018hyz?

what.value: Galactic neutral hydrogen column density in the direction of AT2018hyz ($N_{H,\rm MW}=2.67\times 10^{20}\,\rm{cm^{-2}}$)

evidence.quote: The Galactic neutral hydrogen column density in the direction of AT2018hyz is $N_{H,\rm MW}=2.67\times 10^{20}\,\rm{cm^{-2}}$ (cite: Kalberla05).

what.value: Black hole mass $M_{\rm BH}\approx 5.2\times 10^{6} M_{\odot}$ for AT2018hyz

evidence.quote: Here we use $M_{\rm BH}\approx 5.2\times 10^{6} M_{\odot}$ for AT2018hyz, as inferred by (cite: Gomez2020).

what.value: Earlier radio observations of AT2018hyz from 972 to 1282 days

evidence.quote: In (cite: p1) we presented observations of AT2018hyz from $\delta_{t} =972- 1282$ days after optical discovery (on 2018 Oct 14)

recipe.goal: Calibrate, image, and extract radio and millimeter flux densities
recipe.method: Calibrate and image VLA, MeerKAT, ATCA, ALMA, and SMA datasets using standard pipelines/tasks, and extract point-source flux densities
assumptions: Point source fit for VLA flux density extraction

recipe.goal: Extract and fit Chandra X-ray spectrum
recipe.method: Reprocess Chandra ACIS-S exposures, detect source with wavdetect, extract spectra with specextract, and simultaneously fit an absorbed power-law model in Xspec
key_parameters: 1.5'' source region radius and 30'' background region radius
assumptions: Galactic column density $N_{H,\rm MW}=2.67\times 10^{20}\,\rm{cm^{-2}}$ and intrinsic absorption $N_{H, \rm int} = 0\,\rm{cm^{-2}}$

recipe.goal: Fit multi-frequency radio/mm Spectral Energy Distributions (SEDs)
recipe.method:
Fit each epoch's SED with a weighted Granot & Sari (2002) synchrotron model accounting for both $
u_a \ll 
u_m$ and $
u_m \ll 
u_a$ regimes

recipe.goal: Derive physical outflow parameters for spherical geometry via equipartition analysis
recipe.method: Minimum energy equipartition analysis using SED peak parameters and cooling break constraint from combined radio+mm+Chandra SED
key_parameters: Fixed $\nu_p=2.9$ GHz (with 0.6 GHz RMS propagated into errors), $p=2.16$, $\epsilon_B = 10^{-3}$, launch time $t_0=622$ days

recipe.goal: Model off-axis relativistic jet scenarios (generalized equipartition and structured jet forward modeling)
recipe.method: Apply generalized off-axis equipartition analysis of Matsumoto & Piran (2023) using $\nu_m$ constraint, and forward model afterglow emission from a steep angular structured jet
assumptions: Thin-shell geometry, locally spherical dynamics without lateral spreading, constant density external medium ($k=0$), and ad-hoc $\epsilon_e\propto t^4$ at early times for the structured jet

evidence.quote: While $F_{\nu,p}$ exhibits a steady rise over time (by a factor of $\approx10$), $\nu_p$ remains steady overall (despite some epoch-to-epoch scatter) with a mean value of $2.9\pm 0.7$ GHz
The value of $p$ exhibits some scatter as well, but remains steady, with a mean of $2.16\pm 0.26$; we thus adopt $p=2.16$ in the subsequent analysis.

evidence.quote: The inferred outflow velocity using all epochs is $\beta\approx 0.33$.
We therefore conclude that if AT2018hyz harbors an off-axis jet, then its viewing angle is $\approx 80-90^{\circ}$.

score_reason: All extracted flux densities across all facilities (including ALMA) are tabulated in Table 3, and the analytical equations for the SED fitting (emcee) and equipartition models are explicitly provided or cited from Paper I, making the main SED and equipartition results highly reproducible from the table, though structured jet forward-modeling parameters and ALMA image flux extraction details are incomplete.
rediscovery_reason: The ALMA project 2021.1.01210.T is public, calibrated with the standard CASA pipeline, and the continuum flux densities and subsequent MCMC SED fits and equipartition parameters are numeric and clearly tabulated.
